title: People Ops Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Elena Rodriguez
body:
Overview

This guide consolidates Redwood Inference's standard practices for hiring, employee onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, people-ops partners, and people managers to ensure a consistent, inclusive, and legally compliant employee lifecycle.

Use this as the canonical reference for: interview stages and scorecards, offer approval flows, pre-boarding and 30/60/90 onboarding plans, cadence and artifacts for continuous feedback, promotion and calibration guidance, and templates for common manager workflows.

1) Hiring process (high-level)

Purpose: hire quickly while maintaining quality, fairness, and a strong candidate experience.

- Ownership: hiring manager owns role definition and final hiring decision; people-ops owns posting, offer operations, and compliance checks.
- Target timeline: 4-6 weeks from requisition approval to offer acceptance for IC roles; extend by 1-2 weeks for senior/lead roles.

Stages and SLAs:
1. Requisition and role definition (HR/manager) — Target: 3 business days to post after receiving approvals.
2. Resume screen / recruiter phone screen — Target: 2 business days per batch; average candidate response time goal: 24-48 hours.
3. Hiring manager screen (30 min) — Target: scheduled within 5 business days.
4. Technical assessment (if applicable) — Take-home or timed exercise; standard window: 72 hours to complete.
5. Onsite / loop interviews — 2-4 interviews, 2-3 hours total, culminating in a decision meeting.
6. Decision & debrief — Hiring panel to provide feedback within 2 business days of loop completion.
7. Offer approval & extension — People-ops generates offer within 1 business day after approval.

Offer approval matrix (examples):
- Base compensation within band: hiring manager + people-ops approval.
- Above band up to +10%: requires hiring manager + people-ops + compensation lead.
- Exception > +10% or equity changes: requires VP people-ops + finance approval.

Interview panel composition and fairness rules:
- Minimum 3 interviewers for IC levels (one hiring manager, one peer, one cross-functional or EQ reviewer).
- At least one interviewer trained in inclusive interviewing.
- No interview panel should consist solely of the hiring manager's direct reports.
- Use rubric-based scorecards; written feedback required within 48 hours.

Hiring scorecard (required fields):
- Role fit: "Core skills" (weighted 30%), "System design / depth" (20%), "Problem solving" (20%), "Collaboration and communication" (15%), "Ownership and execution" (10%), "Cultural add / values" (5%).

2) Interview feedback and debrief (process)

1. Each interviewer completes the standardized scorecard in Greenhouse (or recruiting ATS) within 48 hours.
2. Hiring manager consolidates feedback and schedules a 45-minute debrief within 2 business days.
3. Decision documented in ATS; people-ops notified to prepare offer or rejection.
4. Rejection communications: aim to send within 5 business days of decision; provide constructive feedback when requested.

3) Pre-boarding & onboarding (first 90 days)

Goal: accelerate new hire productivity and connection to team, culture, and systems.

Pre-boarding (between offer acceptance and first day):
- People-ops checklist: send welcome packet, confirm start date, collect paperwork (tax forms, direct deposit), and set up benefits enrollment window.
- IT checklist: order and ship hardware within 5 business days; ensure MDM and email accounts are provisioned 48 hours before start.
- Manager checklist: create 30-60-90 plan, assign buddy, prepare role-specific access requests.

Day 0-7 (orientation and access):
- Company orientation: benefits overview, security and acceptable use training, compliance, and company values session.
- Team onboarding: team intro, goals for first week, setup of dev environment or role tools.
- Mandatory trainings: security awareness, data handling policy, and code of conduct.

Week 2-4 (ramp and context):
- Assign first project: small, well-scoped task with clear success criteria.
- 1:1 weekly cadence established between manager and new hire.
- Checkpoint at 30 days: manager completes 30-day checkpoint form and shares feedback.

30/60/90 framework summary (examples):
- 30 days: Understand systems, complete core trainings, deliver first small task.
- 60 days: Contribute to a team project, own a small feature or process, demonstrate cross-team collaboration.
- 90 days: Full ownership of a regular area of work, present a retro/learned-notes session to the team.

Onboarding checklist (short table):
| Item | Owner | Target date |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Welcome email + docs | people-ops | 0 days post-acceptance |
| Hardware shipped | IT | 5 business days pre-start |
| Account provisioning | IT | 48 hours pre-start |
| 30/60/90 plan created | Manager | Before day 1 |
| First 1:1 scheduled | Manager | Day 1 |

4) Performance and feedback cycle

Purpose: create regular, evidence-based feedback loops aligned with company goals and values.

Cadence and artifacts:
- Continuous feedback: encouraged at any time using the performance portal; managers should provide real-time feedback on observable behaviors.
- Weekly 1:1s: recommended frequency; set an agenda and leave notes.
- Quarterly check-ins: manager documents progress vs goals, clarity on priorities, and development needs.
- Annual performance review: data collection window (two weeks), manager narrative, peer input, and calibration meetings.

Quarterly goals (OKRs):
- Role-level objectives set collaboratively with manager; measure progress in quarterly check-ins.

Performance rating and calibration:
- Rating scale: Exceeds expectations / Meets expectations / Needs improvement.
- Calibration: managers attend a calibration panel with HR & senior leadership to review distributions and ensure consistency.
- Promotion cycle: nominations go through manager -> skip-level review -> calibration committee -> people-ops for final approval.

Performance improvement plan (PIP) summary:
- Trigger: sustained performance concerns after coaching and documented checkpoints (typically 60-90 days of concern).
- Duration: standard PIP length is 60 days, with clear success measures and weekly manager check-ins.
- Outcomes: improved performance (return to normal coaching cadence), extension with documented rationale, or separation if outcomes are not met.

5) Manager responsibilities (operational checklist)

- Hiring:
  - Draft clear role requirements and success criteria before opening role.
  - Participate in interview calibration and ensure panels are diverse.
  - Complete hiring decision and feedback within 48 hours of final interview.
- Onboarding:
  - Create 30/60/90 plan and share with the new hire prior to start.
  - Assign buddy and ensure first 1:1 occurs on Day 1.
  - Validate access to tools and systems within 3 business days.
- People development & performance:
  - Schedule weekly 1:1s and quarterly career conversations.
  - Maintain evidence-based notes for performance reviews.
  - Initiate coaching early — document expectations and checkpoints.
- Offboarding:
  - Complete knowledge transfer, revoke access, and ensure exit interview scheduled by people-ops.

6) Templates and examples (copy and use)

- Interview scorecard fields (example):
  - Technical competency (scale 1-5)
  - Problem solving (1-5)
  - System design (1-5 if applicable)
  - Communication and collaboration (1-5)
  - Hiring recommendation (Strong hire / Hire / No hire)

- Manager 30/60/90 template (example):
  - 30 days: key learning goals, stakeholders met, systems accessed.
  - 60 days: deliverables, cross-team dependencies, measurable outcomes.
  - 90 days: ownership areas, impact metrics, growth plan.

- Performance review rubric (guidance): attach concrete examples of evidence for each rating. Ensure alignment to company values (customer-first, engineering excellence, ownership, inclusivity).

7) Legal, compliance, and confidentiality notes

- Background checks: required for roles with access to customer data or sensitive systems; people-ops initiates after a conditional offer.
- International hires: coordinate with people-ops for work authorization, local law compliance, and tax considerations.
- Confidential compensation discussions: only share offer details on a need-to-know basis.

8) Escalation paths and exceptions

- Compensation exceptions: escalate to Head of People + Finance.
- Hiring disputes (panel disagreement): escalate to hiring manager's manager and people-ops to adjudicate.
- Onboarding delays > 5 business days for access: escalate to IT manager and operations lead.

9) Related pages and resources

- Recruiting playbook and ATS instructions (link in related pages).
- Manager hiring checklist template (confluence attachment).
- Performance review timeline calendar (shared team calendar).

Appendix: Useful links and artifacts

- Interview training deck (mandatory for interviewers)
- Diversity & inclusion interviewing guidance
- Sample offer letter templates (region-specific)
- 30/60/90 plan template (copyable)

Change log:
- 2024-07-01: initial published version.
- 2025-06-12: clarified offer approval matrix and added standard interview rubric weights.
- 2026-01-15: updated onboarding hardware lead times and standardized PIP duration to 60 days.
